subject: Apex Health renewal: harmonize term + auto-renew exemption request

Cc: Andrew Chen <andrew.chen@apex.health>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Agreement term and billing cadence for Apex Health renewal

Marissa,

We had a brief procurement touchpoint this morning — they want to align the upcoming Redwood contract to our fiscal year and also consolidate the new enterprise seats into the same term. Two asks: 1) can we co-term the renewal to 2027-06-30 instead of the anniversary date, and 2) procurement prefers a single annual invoice (one PO) rather than quarterly billing. They mentioned an auto-renew clause is acceptable but need a one-time opt-out window at 60 days.

Also flagged that they may move forward with additional seats (approx +20%) in Q1, so any guidance on ramping usage and credits would help.

Can you confirm next steps and timeline for legal and DocuSign?

Thanks,
Sally James
Sourcing Lead, ProcureCorp

Attachments: none
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Agreement term and billing cadence for Apex Health renewal

Hi Sally / Andrew — thanks for the heads up. Quick recap + proposal below so we have a single place to track: 

- Co-term target: move renewal to 2027-06-30 (aligns with Apex FY).
- Billing cadence: one annual invoice preferred; Redwood can accommodate with net-30 payment terms.
- Auto-renew: we can include an auto-renew clause with a 60-day opt-out window; we'll flag this for legal review for explicit language.
- Ramp & seats: if Apex commits to +20% seats at renewal, we can propose a 24-month term with a staged ramp (months 1–6 at 60% of committed capacity, months 7–18 step up to 100%). We typically offer an early-burst credit to smooth unit economics during the ramp — options in attached Pricing_Scenarios.xlsx.

Rishi / Kim / Lauren — please review finance & legal bullets, the attached draft renewal, and confirm whether the frontloaded credit (Option B in the spreadsheet) is workable. Also note: procurement will want a single PO + DocuSign. I’ve attached an initial draft (Apex_Renewal_Draft_202609.pdf) for legal to redline.

Sally — can you confirm the procurement contact and preferred PO timeline? Andrew — are there any technical constraints that would affect the ramp timing?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Agreement term and billing cadence for Apex Health renewal

Thanks for pulling this together, Marissa. A few finance notes after reviewing the draft and scenarios: 

- Term structure: Finance prefers a 24-month committed term to give us runway for the ramp and to amortize onboarding credits. We can still set the contract co-term to 2027-06-30 via a 24-month term that frontloads the earliest months into year one (we'll document exact dates in the SOW).
- Billing: One annual invoice is fine if procurement provides a single PO covering the full term. We need confirmation of the PO value and an approver signature on the SOW prior to DocuSign.
- Credit structure: Option B (frontloaded credit of 30% of year-1 expected token spend, applied across Q1–Q2) looks clean and preserves margin. If Apex wants a steeper frontload we can do a one-time onboarding credit but would need senior approval (finance_elevate).
- Auto-renew: we can add a 60-day opt-out window. Any auto-renew price protection or step increase needs to be explicit in the renewal terms.

I’ll slot this for a quick review with finance on Monday. Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Strategic Accounts — Finance Liaison, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — this plan looks sensible. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Co-term: 2027-06-30 is preferred. Procurement confirms they will issue a single PO but need the final contract value by 2026-09-20 to process in their FY planning window.
- Seats: we expect to sign for +20% seats at renewal but will likely only enable ~60% of that capacity in Q1 and then ramp to full usage by month 9 after go-live. Your staged ramp proposal maps well to this.
- DocuSign & PO: procurement wants to see the DocuSign envelope before issuing the PO (internal rule). Can you include a clause that explicitly notes an opt-out period of 60 days prior to renewal?

Quick question for Rishi: any of the proposed quotas or burst allowances create infra constraints we should be aware of during months 1–3?

Appreciate the clarity — Andrew
